---
title: "if stops on an empty or NA condition"
ref: FLW-08
categories: [Control flow]
impact: cryptique
extrait: 'if (NA) "yes"'
attendu: "the branch to be simply skipped"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
threshold <- NA
if (5 > threshold) {
  "above"
}

found <- grepl("z", x = character(0))
found
if (found) {
  "found"
}
```
:::

## Why

`if` demands exactly one value, `TRUE` or `FALSE`. A comparison with `NA` gives `NA`, and R refuses to choose: "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed". An empty vector, such as the `logical(0)` that `grepl()` returns on an empty input, gives "argument is of length zero".

Both cases happen with real data: a missing value in a file, a filter that keeps no rows. The code has run a hundred times, then stops the day a value is missing.

## The fix

`isTRUE()` and `isFALSE()` always return a single value, `FALSE` for `NA` or for an empty vector. When these cases deserve their own handling, test for them first.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
isTRUE(5 > threshold)
isTRUE(found)

if (isTRUE(5 > threshold)) {
  "above"
} else {
  "unknown or below"
}
```
:::
